title: Probabilistic rollout forecast canvas and decision aid for staged releases
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a lightweight visual canvas inside the Redwood Console that surfaces probabilistic forecasts for staged rollouts (canary, A/B, traffic-splits). The canvas aims to give product owners and SREs a concise prediction of risk/benefit over time under uncertainty, allow scenario comparison, and provide quick rollback recommendations with confidence bands. The prototype should be interactive (drag exposure, toggle metrics, adjust sample size) and integrate with existing rollout controls and guardrails.
background_and_rationale: Current rollout views are deterministic: traffic % and binary pass/fail signals. Teams have requested a way to see "what could happen" given noisy signals and sampling variance, especially for small canaries or short-lived experiments. A probabilistic forecast helps quantify the chance of hitting error budgets, SLA breaches, or cost thresholds, and supports better decisions about ramp speed and abort conditions.
design_goals: 1) Make uncertainty visible without overwhelming the user. 2) Support side-by-side scenario comparison (e.g., 5% -> 50% in 24h vs 5% -> 20% in 72h). 3) Surface rollback recommendations with an evidence score. 4) Fit within the Console's existing rollouts panel and be performant for live data.
deliverables: Interactive Figma prototype (canvas with timeline, confidence bands, metric toggles)
Annotated spec doc with UX states and accessibility notes
Copy deck for microcopy and recommended alerts
Handoff package for frontend (react + d3) including component sketches
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates two scenarios compared side-by-side and updates forecasts when exposure is dragged
Confidence bands (50%/90%) are shown for selected primary metric (latency/error rate/cost)
A rollback recommendation card appears when risk probability exceeds configured threshold, with justification text and links to relevant logs/dashboards
Design passes accessibility review (contrast and keyboard interactions) and has developer-ready tokens and spacing specs

design_iterations: V1: simple shaded band around trajectory — rejected for low expressiveness
V2: dual-scenario canvas with 50%/90% bands — chosen for clarity and comparison affordance
V3: added evidence-based rollback card and recommended next steps — final
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use bootstrap-derived confidence bands computed in backend (Data) to avoid misleading analytic approximations on-client
Tradeoff: Adding rich uncertainty visuals increases cognitive load; to mitigate we hide advanced overlays behind a 'Show details' toggle
Decision: Prioritize latency and error-rate as first-class metrics; cost included as secondary metric with coarser granularity to reduce compute
Tradeoff: Real-time forecasting requires sampling windows — we will default to 5m/30m windows with ability to adjust, so small canaries show larger bands
review_feedback: PM (Liam Ortiz): like the scenario compare, wants an explicit 'confidence to rollout' score
SRE (Priya Kumar): ensure rollback card links directly to the incident timeline and can trigger safe-stop API
Frontend (Arjun Patel): prefers a modular component to reuse in A/B experiments view
Accessibility (Jordan Li): keyboard focus on timeline scrubber needs clear visible state
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Users misinterpret confidence bands as guarantees — Mitigation: explicit legend and tooltip copy explaining statistical meaning
Risk: Backend compute cost for forecasts at high concurrency — Mitigation: cache recent forecasts and limit live updates to active rollouts only
Risk: Added UI complexity slows rollout tasks — Mitigation: a compact collapsed mode shows only the headline probability and rollback button
